posts.title: Digital Asset Market Clarity Act
posts.label: ⏱️ Cloture motion filed
posts.summary: The bill would create a regulatory framework for digital assets (cryptocurrencies and similar blockchain-based commodities), assigning the Commodity Futures Trading Commission primary oversight of digital commodity exchanges and transactions, while giving the Securities and Exchange Commission jurisdiction over certain digital commodity activities by brokers and dealers. It would exempt digital commodities on mature blockchains from SEC registration if they meet certain requirements, establish trading, recordkeeping, and customer asset protection standards, and require digital asset platforms to comply with anti-money laundering rules. The measure also addresses Federal Reserve restrictions on central bank digital currencies and direct offerings to individuals.
posts.meta: Banking, Housing, and Urban Affairs Committee, Financial Services Committee, Agriculture Committee · Rep. J. Hill (R-AR)
posts.whatsNext: Cloture vote expected on the second session day (60 votes to advance)

posts.title: Doug LaMalfa Federal Disaster Tax Relief Certainty Act
posts.label: ✅🏛️ Passed Senate (unanimous consent)
posts.summary: The bill would extend federal tax breaks for people who suffered losses in major disasters and wildfires. It would allow taxpayers to deduct personal casualty losses from disasters occurring through the end of 2026, and would let people exclude wildfire relief payments from their taxable income if the fires were declared federal disasters between 2015 and 2026, regardless of when they receive the payments.
posts.meta: Finance Committee, Ways and Means Committee · Rep. W. Steube (R-FL)
posts.whatsNext: Presidential review (±10 days)

posts.title: Stop Secret Spending Act of 2025
posts.label: ✅🏛️ Passed Senate (unanimous consent)
posts.summary: The bill would require federal agencies to publicly report spending on "other transaction agreements" (a type of contract that currently operates with less transparency and fewer regulations than standard government contracts) to the USAspending.gov website, where federal spending is tracked. It would also require the Treasury Department to publish annual reports showing how much federal spending data remains unreported and why, and would direct inspector generals at certain agencies to assess their spending data quality for the next decade.
posts.meta: Oversight and Government Reform Committee · Rep. Barry Moore (R-AL)
posts.whatsNext: Presidential review (±10 days)

posts.title: Continuing Appropriations and Extensions Act, 2027
posts.label: ✅🏛️ Passed Senate with amendment (90-6)
posts.summary: The bill would extend duty-free trade preferences for most products from eligible sub-Saharan African countries through the end of 2028, allowing them to export to the U.S. market without tariffs. It would also extend customs user fees through the end of 2031, and would refund tariffs paid on African imports that entered the U.S. between October 2025 and the bill's enactment date.
posts.meta: Ways and Means Committee · Rep. Jason Smith (R-MO)

posts.title: Northern Border Security Enhancement and Review Act
posts.label: ✅🏛️ Passed Senate with amendment (unanimous consent)
posts.summary: The bill would require the Department of Homeland Security to conduct a threat analysis of the northern U.S. border every three years, examining terrorism and criminal threats, apprehension trends, and security improvements needed. It would also mandate that DHS update its northern border security strategy by September 2, 2026, and every five years thereafter based on these analyses, while requiring U.S. Customs and Border Protection to develop metrics to measure how effectively it secures the northern border in remote areas by air and water.

posts.label: 🗳️ Motion to proceed rejected (48-50)
posts.summary: The joint resolution seeks to overturn an Environmental Protection Agency rule that modified when companies must begin reporting and keeping records about certain harmful chemicals known as PFAS (forever chemicals). If passed, it would use congressional authority to disapprove and block the EPA's regulatory change.

posts.title: Protect College Sports Act of 2026
posts.label: ⏱️ Cloture motion filed
posts.summary: The bill would establish federal rules for college athletes' name, image, and likeness (NIL) deals, requiring athletes to disclose compensation above $600 and capping agent fees at 5 percent. It would also allow athletes one penalty-free transfer, restrict how schools can pay athletes to work around revenue-sharing limits, and give schools and conferences limited antitrust protection to collectively negotiate sports broadcasting rights.

posts.title: Youth Poisoning Protection Act
posts.label: ✅🏛️ Passed Senate (voice vote)
posts.summary: The bill would ban the sale of consumer products containing 10% or more sodium nitrite, with exceptions for drugs, medical devices, cosmetics, and food products. It aims to protect young people from accidental or intentional poisoning through access to high-concentration sodium nitrite products.
posts.meta: Commerce, Science, and Transportation Committee · Sen. Tammy Duckworth (D-IL)
posts.whatsNext: To the House (if and when it takes it up)

posts.title: Bankruptcy Threshold Adjustment Act of 2026
posts.label: ✅🏛️ Passed Senate (unanimous consent)
posts.meta: Sen. Chuck Grassley (R-IA)
posts.whatsNext: To the House (if and when it takes it up)

posts.title: Foreign Robocall Elimination Act
posts.label: ✅🏛️ Passed Senate with amendment (unanimous consent)
posts.summary: The bill would establish an interagency task force to advise federal agencies and Congress on combating robocalls originating from outside the United States. It would also extend the term for the Federal Communications Commission's designation of an industry consortium responsible for tracing unlawful robocalls from annual to once every three years.
posts.meta: Commerce, Science, and Transportation Committee · Sen. Ted Budd (R-NC)
posts.whatsNext: To the House (if and when it takes it up)

posts.title: AGOA Extension Act
posts.label: 🗳️ Motion to proceed filed
posts.summary: The bill would extend through the end of 2028 duty-free trade benefits that allow most exports from eligible sub-Saharan African countries to enter the U.S. market without tariffs, while also extending customs user fees through the end of 2031. It would also allow for refunds of duties paid on African imports that entered the country after September 30, 2025.
posts.meta: Ways and Means Committee · Rep. Jason Smith (R-MO)
posts.whatsNext: The Senate votes on taking it up (the motion can be withdrawn)
